production.note: US model years 2026 to present: 'the new 2026 911 Turbo S is the most powerful production 911 to date'; 'Arrival in U.S. Porsche Centers is expected by Spring, 2026.' Launched as the current model in 2025-2026; no later model year page was opened.

body.note: 'Available as a coupe and Cabriolet'. The Cabriolet is the open version of the same variant.

configuration.note: 'the 3.6-liter boxer engine'; C/D panel: 'twin-turbocharged and intercooled DOHC 24-valve 3.6-liter flat-6'.

displacementL.note: Porsche states '3.6-liter'; the C/D panel also says '3.6-liter flat-6'. No cc figure was found on an opened page, so the stated litre figure is used.

aspiration.note: 'two eTurbos are used in the new 911 Turbo S' (electrically assisted turbochargers).

fuel.note: C/D panel: '3.6-liter flat-6, 631 hp, 560 lb-ft + AC motor, 80 hp, 138 lb-ft (combined output: 701 hp, 590 lb-ft; lithium-ion battery pack)'. Porsche T-Hybrid; not a plug-in.

drivetrain.note: '701 hp (523 kW) all-wheel drive sports car'; press kit: 'Porsche Traction Management (PTM) all-wheel drive system'.

transmission.note: 'An eight-speed PDK with an integrated electric motor', the only transmission. DCT is Porsche PDK.

powerHp.note: Combined system output. Quote: "achieves a system output of 701 hp (523 kW)". The combustion engine alone makes 631 hp (press kit pcna-2026-911-turbo-s-press-kit: 'the combustion engine in the new 911 Turbo S develops a power output of 631 hp (471 kW)'). C/D panel (cd-2026-911-turbo-s): '(combined output: 701 hp, 590 lb-ft; ...)'.

weightLb.note: 2026 coupe with the 8-speed PDK (only transmission), manufacturer step 1. Quote: "The new 911 Turbo S has a curb weight of 3,829 lbs." No Cabriolet figure was given (press kit power-to-weight: '5.5 lb./hp (Cabriolet: 5.7 lb./hp)'). Car and Driver's road-test panel gives 3,833 lb (see discrepancies).
